The ratings map for Beijer Ref
Every answer the Investment Analyst wrote in the four layers behind this memo, word for word
The Financial Analyst Memo: every financial table and model output behind this memo
Beijer Ref (BEIJ.B-SE) · Investment memo

Beijer Ref is a sound compounder of earnings at about 12% a year whose good news is now in the share price; the better-skewed entry point is likely to come around the summer of 2027

As at 9 November 2026. Price SEK 156.3 (6 November 2026). Money in SEK millions unless stated; per-share figures in SEK.

All leverage figures in this memo correct a timing error in the model's year-end net debt. The bases of the forecasts and of consensus, and that correction, are set out in the end notes.

0. Summary of key insights, implications and conclusions

The case in one paragraph. Beijer Ref is the world's largest wholesaler of refrigeration and air-conditioning parts and equipment to professional installers. Aftermarket demand makes up 80 to 90% of its sales; it leads in Europe and is a small but fast-growing consolidator in North America. In five months, four forces moved in Beijer Ref's favour at once: organic growth turned positive, the acquisition engine restarted, a permanent chief executive was appointed, and a long-term industrial owner replaced a private-equity seller. The result is a sound earnings compounder under stable ownership: EPS rises about 13% in 2026 and about 12% a year to 2030, and deals already signed supply over half of the EPS growth to 2027. The open question is no longer whether the business works. The open question is what the market will pay for Beijer Ref's earnings, and when.

The chain of reasoning in four steps.

1. The business worksEPS grows about 12% a year, and signed deals supply over half of the growth to FY2027.
→
2. Expectations have caught upThe shares rose 27% in six months, and the model sits 4 to 6% below FY2027 consensus EPS.
→
3. The test comes lateThe July and October 2027 reports face the record summer of 2026; the two reports before them are easy.
→
4. Wait for the better entryThe skew improves around the summer of 2027, or earlier if the multiple falls to 19x to 20x.

Six conclusions.

1
Beijer Ref's earnings are predictable; its organic-growth prints and its multiple are not.
The model puts FY2027 EPS at SEK 6.51, with eight outcomes in ten within about 6% either side. No single operating assumption moves FY2027 EPS by more than about 3%.
2
Market expectations have caught up with the business.
Like for like, the model is 4 to 6% below FY2027 consensus EPS, and about 3 points of that gap can surface as cuts. I put the chance that FY2027 results meet or beat today's consensus at between one in four and one in three. After a 27% rise in the share price in six months, the positives are known and largely priced.
3
The skew lies in the sequence of reports, not in the level of earnings.
Two easy reports come first (29 January and late April 2027). Two hard reports follow in July and October 2027, against the record summer of 2026. Then 2028 is easier: the comparisons are soft, the 2029 product ban comes into view and two more years of acquisitions are added. FY2027 estimate revisions should therefore trace a V.
4
The model's headline return needs a multiple that I do not think the evidence supports.
At the guideline fair multiple of 34.26x, the model returns +82.5% to 31 March 2028, and three-fifths of that return is the multiple. I believe the earnings leg (about +20%). At 24x to 26x, the multiple I would use in a delivery phase, the return is +28% to +40%; at an unchanged multiple it is +22%; and a stall that coincides with a de-rating of the Swedish serial acquirers gives about nil. Over three years the supportable return is about 15 to 18% a year.
5
The unpriced positives concern the use of capital, not demand.
Four levers sit in no forecast: inventory (about 165 days, against about 90 at Watsco), a sharper return-on-capital target, a second European cost programme and the pay-off from private label in North America. The new owner's habits point at exactly these four levers.
6
The unpriced negatives concern financing, not operations.
Consensus has net interest falling when it will rise. SEK 3.4bn of option liabilities (the cost of buying out stakes left with sellers) sit outside net debt, so all-in leverage is about 2.8x against about 2.0x reported. Leverage peaks in the second quarter of each year. And no broker's numbers carry the Q3 2027 organic growth of about zero that the model expects.

The five judgements that move the value of the shares most (the arithmetic is in topic 9):

Judgement in the forecastsPlausible errorEffect on EPS
The summer of 2027 is normal, so Q3 2027 organic growth is about zero4 points either wayFY2027 plus or minus 2.7%
The krona holds near EUR/SEK 11.25% either wayFY2027 plus or minus 2.5%

The multiple outweighs all five judgements: each turn of the P/E is worth about 5% of the share price, and the plausible range of the multiple moves the share price about three times as far as the plausible range of earnings.
Where the skew would become unusually positive. Any one of four trackable events would change the character of the case: (a) a numerical target for return on capital or working capital from the new chief executive and owner; (b) an entry multiple near 19x to 20x, at which earnings growth alone carries the return; (c) the Q3 2027 report published, with estimates already cut; (d) acquisitions above the base pace, funded by a release of inventory rather than by debt.

1Tailwinds and headwinds in the operating environment

Conclusion: the operating environment is moderately favourable for Beijer Ref's earnings and unfavourable for its multiple; regulation, the best-dated tailwind, reaches comfort cooling, the largest segment, only in 2029.

Evidence.

Tailwinds: they act on operations
  • Demand has turned in the reported numbers. Organic growth ran -1.4%, about 0%, +1% and +8.3% over the four quarters to Q3 2026. In Q3 it was +12.5% in EMEA (Europe, the Middle East and Africa), +3.4% in North America and +0.2% in Asia-Pacific. Organic order intake rose 12%, and book-to-bill was 1.03x against a three-year average of 0.97x (DNB Carnegie).
  • Part of the turn is structural and dated in law. The EU quota for fluorinated gases (F-gases) halves on 1 January 2027. From the same date, new split air-to-water units using refrigerants with a global warming potential (GWP) above 150 are banned, and split air-to-air units follow in January 2029. The US phases down hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) by 85% by 2036. Beijer Ref's own manufacturing of natural-refrigerant systems grew 19% organically in Q3, after 25% in Q2. Air-conditioning penetration is 23% in Europe against 93% in the US.
  • Part of the turn is cyclical. Comfort cooling (about 62% of sales) drove Q3 in the warmest Western European summer on record. Price added only about 2% to growth, and on our estimate the weather supplied about SEK 450m of Q3 sales.
  • Currency has flipped from headwind to tailwind. The krona has weakened to about EUR/SEK 11.20, against an expected 10.40 to 10.50. Currency translation took SEK 209m off EBITA in 2025; it now adds to EBITA for two to three quarters.
Headwinds: one of them acts on the multiple
  • Two cyclical headwinds are bottoming, not lifting. US homeowners are deferring the replacement of systems: mortgage rates are above 7%, system prices are up 70 to 100% since 2019, and 48% of US distributors name repair instead of replacement as their largest headwind. European construction is contracting.
  • Rising interest rates are hostile, and they act on the multiple. The US ten-year yield is above 5%; the Riksbank raised its policy rate to 2.00% in November; the European Central Bank is expected to raise its rate in December, with eurozone inflation at 4.0%; and the market is risk-off beneath an index at its high.
  • Competition is rising at the edges. Home Depot has built a US distribution arm for heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC) equipment through three acquisitions; Watsco has missed on gross margin twice in 2026; and Chinese propane-based units reach Europe at about 30% lower ex-warehouse cost (Jefferies).

Inference. The tailwinds act on operations and are visible for years; the main headwind acts on the price the market pays for the earnings.

About half of the Q3 2026 acceleration was weather, so the same quarter of 2027 will show an optical reversal. Regulation directly touches about 40 to 45% of sales today and does not reach comfort cooling until 2029. Refrigerants are now only 2 to 3% of sales (over 15% in 2018), so the 2027 quota step is a nudge worth about SEK 40m, not a repeat of the 2018 windfall.

Cheap Asian propane units cut both ways for a distributor. Lower prices passed through to customers shrink gross profit in kronor, but the same units are a ready supply of private-label product, and they hurt European manufacturers far more than they hurt the distribution channel.

So what. Build the forecasts on organic growth of 3 to 5%, not on EMEA's Q3 rate; treat currency as a two-way risk; and carry the macro risk in the multiple, not in the earnings.
Strongest counter-case. Jefferies argues that the turn is "more than a hot summer": growth was led by volume, and activity held through September and early October. Six of the last nine European summers have been called hot, and each hot summer enlarges the installed base of units that need parts and service. If Jefferies is right, organic growth in 2027 is nearer 5% than 3%.
What would change my view. Organic growth above 6% in Q4 2026 and Q1 2027, the two quarters with no weather effect, together with North American growth above 5%, would show a structural turn. Organic growth below 3% in Q4 2026, against an easy base, would show the reverse.
Against the market. The two brokers whose research we can see read Q3 as the start of a stronger cycle. I agree on the direction and differ on the rate: the dependable organic rate is 3 to 5%. The market also gives too little weight to how firmly today's higher interest rates hold down the multiples of the Swedish serial acquirers.

Score: 65, set by the Rater. A real, partly structural positive: law-dated F-gas steps (quota halving January 2027, split-unit bans 2027 and 2029, US HFC phase-down) reach about 40-45% of sales and European AC penetration is 23% against 93% in the US, but about half of Q3's +8.3% organic was a record summer that reverses in 2027, the regulation reaches comfort cooling (62% of sales) only in 2029, US replacement and European construction are bottoming rather than lifting, the krona gain is temporary and two-way, and Home Depot and cheap Chinese propane units press at the edges (rates act on the multiple and are scored in 9, 11 and 12). Coherent with the External group's 64; clearly more dated and structural than OEM International's modestly positive Nordic distribution recovery, short of Eckert & Ziegler's regulatory-barrier structural demand.

2Internally-driven corporate change forces

Conclusion: the internal forces are strong and aligned on ownership and execution, but they have not yet raised Beijer Ref's ambition or its returns.

Evidence.

  • A long-term industrial owner now controls the company. Melker Schörling AB bought all the A-shares on 11 June 2026 (14.1% of the votes on 2.1% of the capital) and said it intends to increase its stake; it has disclosed no further purchases since. EQT then placed its remaining 30.7m B-shares (6.4% of the capital) on 18 June 2026 for about EUR 370m. On that evidence the overhang of shares for sale has gone, as well as the private-equity control (the source is discussed in end note 5).
  • The top layer of management is new but internal. Per Bertland, chief executive until 2021, became chair in April 2026. Jonas Steen, who has run EMEA (about 60% of the group) since 2010, became chief executive on 1 November 2026 and keeps the EMEA role until a successor is found.
  • The acquisition engine is running above its normal pace. Deals signed in nine months add about SEK 3.7bn of annual sales (about 10% of 2025 revenue), against a stated normal pace of SEK 2.5bn to 3.5bn a year. Enertrak brings Canada, FG Europe (pending approval) brings south-east Europe, and Refra brings the manufacture of natural-refrigerant systems.
  • Execution has measurably improved. The SEK 100m European consolidation programme is at its full run-rate; the Sinclair private label is in 90 of 130 North American branches, up from about 30 a year ago; and SCM Frigo has added second shifts.
  • The financial framework was tightened, not raised. The leverage ceiling came down to below 2.5x net debt to EBITDA, from below 3x, and a target for operating cash flow of 80 to 90% of adjusted EBITA was added. The 2023 growth and margin targets were only reaffirmed.
  • The changes have costs. North American branch openings and the private-label roll-out took 20 to 30 basis points off the group margin in Q3, and the share of manufactured sales using low-GWP refrigerants slipped from 66% to 62% in one quarter.

Inference. The changes concern who owns and leads Beijer Ref and how hard its plan is executed; they do not change what the company aims to achieve.

The new owner's other holdings indicate what probably comes next for Beijer Ref:

Melker Schörling holdingWhat its financial framework targets
SecuritasThe same two numbers that Beijer Ref has just added: a leverage ceiling and a cash-conversion target
HexagonReturn on capital of about 15%; acquisitions must earn their cost of capital within three years
Assa Abloy5% organic growth plus 5% acquired growth

I read the three frameworks as a house style: about 10% growth, with discipline on returns and cash. The files do not date Beijer Ref's framework change against the owner's arrival, so the pattern is suggestive rather than proof. On that pattern, the next change to Beijer Ref's targets is more likely to be a sharper target for returns or cash, possibly with a more modest growth range, than a raised growth ambition.

So what. The internal forces underwrite the earnings path (signed deals alone add about 6.5% to FY2027 revenue) and hold an unpriced option on higher returns. They do not justify assuming a raised margin target, a buyback or a faster pace of acquisitions.
Strongest counter-case. Jefferies expects an upgrade of the targets in Q1 2027, and a Q3 underlying EBITA margin of 11.9% makes the target corridor of 10 to 12% look low. The opposite risk is also real: an owner who prefers to conserve capital could slow debt-funded deals, which would lower EPS growth from 2028.
What would change my view. On 29 January 2027, a numerical target for return on capital or working capital, or a second efficiency programme, would make the internal force stronger than I assume. A pause in acquisitions, or a large clear-the-decks charge without a plan, would make it weaker.
Against the market. The market narrative treats the new owner and the new chief executive as wholly positive, and the balance sheet as ample "firepower" for acquisitions. I agree on continuity. I differ on what comes next (discipline before ambition) and on the size of the firepower (topic 5).

Score: 64, set by the Rater. Several aligned internal moves in five months: a long-term industrial owner (Melker Schörling) replacing the EQT overhang, an internal chief executive who ran EMEA, an acquisition engine re-lit above its normal pace (about SEK 3.7bn of sales signed, some 10% of revenue, supplying about 55% of EPS growth to FY2027), the SEK 100m programme at full run-rate and Sinclair private label in 90 of 130 US branches; but ambition and returns are unchanged, deals now earn only about 7-9% on new capital, the leverage ceiling governs the pace and the US roll-out costs 20-30bp of margin. Above Richard's 'gently positive but mediocre' CVS (55) because the deals reach earnings within three years, a little above the Internal group's 60; close to OEM International, whose new owner turned it into an active acquirer with a record margin, which Beijer Ref does not yet match.

3Industry structure, competitive advantage, financial profile and management

Conclusion: Beijer Ref's industry structure and moats are good and widening, but its financial profile and governance are average, and the gap between the two is why the stock deserves a mid-range rather than a premium multiple.

Evidence.

  • The industry structure favours a technically capable consolidator. Customers are fragmented (more than 100,000 installers); distributors price for margin (prices rose while volumes fell from 2023 to 2025); and branch density, exclusive brand rights, refrigerant quotas and training hold back new entrants. Market share drifts to the distributors with scale and technical capability.
  • Beijer Ref's position is strong in Europe and thin in the US. It is number one in Europe and in Australia and New Zealand, but it holds only about 1 to 1.5% of a USD 70bn to 100bn North American market in which Watsco holds 10% or more.
  • Most of Beijer Ref's moats are widening. Training for flammable and high-pressure refrigerants, private label (25 to 30% of EMEA's HVAC sales) and own green manufacturing (about 8 to 10% of group sales) all grow with each regulatory step and each deal. One moat is narrowing: the profit on refrigerant refills.
  • The financial profile is ordinary, as the table below shows.
MeasureBeijer RefComparison
EBITA marginAbout 11%14 to 23% for the Swedish serial acquirers
Return on operating capital (twelve months to Q3 2026)11.2%Below the company's target of above 12% and its ten-year average of 14.7% before the US entry; about half the 19 to 22% of Lifco, Addtech and Indutrade
Working capital (FactSet's definition)About 40% of salesInventory alone is about 165 days, against about 90 at Watsco
Free cash flow, 2021 to 2025-49% to +132% of net incomeVolatile from year to year
  • The ambition is large and the strategy coherent. The stated aim, set in 2023, is to double the company in five to seven years; our forecast path gets about 93% of the way by 2030. The method is to buy local distributors, keep their managers and brands, and add purchasing scale, private label and green manufacturing on top. The culture is decentralised and entrepreneurial. It shows strain where the US business meets the group, and staff turnover is 17%, against 12 to 14% at Lifco and Indutrade.
  • Management is capable, but governance is below the standard of the Swedish serial acquirers. The tenured operating team delivered scale, margin and cash through a weak market. The new chief executive is unproven as the allocator of the group's capital. The company has a dual-class share structure, no central internal audit across more than 170 subsidiaries, and a long-term incentive plan weighted 90% to growth in profit per share, with nothing on return on capital. Both platform acquisitions needed new equity.

Inference. Beijer Ref is a well-moated distributor, not a high-return compounder. Its floor is durable and its runway is long: the market is many times the company's size, so capital and the capacity to integrate deals limit growth, not demand. But each krona of added sales needs about 40 öre of working capital, plus goodwill.

The price paid for acquisitions is the weak link in the returns. The forecasts assume deals at about 0.85x sales, but the option liabilities booked for the stakes left with sellers imply prices well above that, and the net-debt path in the earlier answer sets is consistent with prices of 1.15x to 1.25x sales. At those prices the after-tax return on new capital is about 7 to 9%, not far above the cost of capital.

So what. Returns, not growth, explain Beijer Ref's discount to the best Swedish compounders, so capital efficiency is the route to closing the discount. The arithmetic is encouraging: taking 5 points of revenue out of working capital releases about SEK 2.3bn on FY2027 revenue of SEK 45,539m. That release alone lifts return on operating capital from about 11.5% to about 12.1%, and it would fund roughly SEK 2bn of acquired sales without new debt.
Strongest counter-case. Organic growth under EQT (8.6% a year from 2021 to 2024) beat the serial acquirers' 7.0% (DNB Carnegie), and Beijer Ref's aftermarket base is more defensive than theirs. On that view the market wrongly prices a compounder as a cyclical distributor, and the discount should close on delivery alone.
What would change my view. Upward: inventory days falling toward 140 with service levels intact, an incentive plan that rewards return on capital, or an internal audit function. Downward: a control failure in a subsidiary, or a North American margin that has not recovered by 2028.
Against the market. I agree with the market that a discount is warranted. I differ on how the discount closes: brokers argue for a re-rating on growth and delivery, whereas I think it closes only if returns rise, and the owner most likely to push for higher returns has just arrived.

Score: 57, set by the Rater. Qualitatively good and widening: a fragmented customer base, distributors that price for margin, number one in Europe and ANZ, moats in training, private label and green manufacturing that grow with each regulatory step, and a margin held at 10.6-10.7% through the 2023-25 stall; but the financial profile is ordinary (ROIC 7.7% p56, gross margin p10, EBITDA margin p27, return on operating capital 11.2% below its 12% target and half the Swedish compounders'), new capital earns about 7-9% after tax, close to its cost, working capital is about 40% of sales, the US position is sub-scale and governance (no internal audit, LTI on EPS only) trails the cohort. Coherent with the groups (65, 63, 48, 60); well above IMCD's leveraged, downgraded specialty distribution, below Helios Towers whose new capital earns far more.

4Conservatism of guidance and the record of delivery

Conclusion: Beijer Ref's guidance is a framework with no low bar in it; the dependable upgrades come from acquisitions, not from sandbagged targets.

Evidence.

There is no annual guidance. The framework is the set of five-year targets from November 2023. The table sets each target against the model's forecast path.

  • The delivery record splits cleanly between what Beijer Ref controls and what it does not. The company delivers what it controls: the margin held at 10.6 to 10.7% through the organic stall of 2023 to 2025, the savings programme landed on plan, and Q3 2026 beat consensus by 6% on sales and by 6 to 8% on EBITA. It misses on what the weather and US housing control: organic growth was below 3% for four quarters to mid-2026.
  • Consensus has been early in calling the organic recovery. Consensus FY2026 EPS fell from SEK 6.25 to SEK 5.41 before recovering.
  • Acquisitions are the standing source of upgrades. Acquisitions have added about 10% a year to EBITA for a decade, and brokers count each one only when it completes.

Inference. Beijer Ref's conservatism is real but passive: it comes from silence and cautious words, not from a low number. The framework is conservative on one measure (margin) and stretching on three (organic growth, cash conversion and return on capital), so it is not a low bar. The stretch does no harm only because there is no annual figure to miss.

So what. Beats come from deals, hot summers and margin; misses come from organic growth in the winter quarters. Without guidance, each report is judged on organic growth against broker assumptions that differ widely, so the quarterly prints are noisier than the underlying earnings.
Strongest counter-case. A company that gives no guidance, and whose consensus forecasts exclude its main growth engine, upgrades structurally by construction. DNB Carnegie says Beijer Ref "typically outperforms consensus as unannounced M&A is not modelled".
What would change my view. A raised margin corridor or the introduction of annual guidance would be a first for the company. An explicit tempering of the organic half of the growth target would be the first downward change to the framework since 2023.
Against the market. Jefferies expects a target upgrade in Q1 2027. I put the chance of reaffirmation on 29 January at about three in four, and of a raised margin corridor at 10 to 15%. A chief executive three months into the job, who still runs EMEA and whose company meets only two of six targets cleanly, is more likely to reaffirm the targets and add discipline.

Score: 49, set by the Rater. No annual guidance (neutral); against its own 2023 targets it meets margin and leverage but has missed the organic half every year since 2023 and is borderline on return and cash conversion, and consensus FY2026 EPS fell from SEK 6.25 to 5.41 during the organic stall before the Q3 2026 beat of 6% on sales and 6-8% on EBITA; deals are the standing source of upgrades but nothing is sandbagged. Between the Guidance (52) and Sell-side estimates (46) groups; below CVS Group, which largely met its targets, and level with Sdiptech's mixed record.

5Pricing power, operating leverage, financial leverage, cost-out and feedback loops

Conclusion: in Beijer Ref, revenue growth converts into profit growth at about one for one, so outsized profit growth has to come from deploying capital and using it more efficiently, not from operating leverage or price.

Evidence and mechanism: each profit lever, one by one.

LeverWhat the evidence showsNet effect
Operating leverageLow over a year and high within it. Incremental EBITA margins were about 10% in Q2 2026 and 12.5% in Q3, close to the average margin, and the drop-through on organic volume is 15 to 20%. Organic growth of 8.3% in Q3 came with an underlying margin 20 basis points below Q2's. The mirror image is resilience: in 2020 revenue fell 5.1% and the margin fell by less than a point. Within the year, winter-quarter margins sit 4 to 5 points below summer ones.Steadiness, not margin-led upgrades
Pricing powerPass-through, not real price. Price adds about 2% to growth now and about 1.5% later. Price protects gross profit in kronor, but with wages rising 3 to 4% a year it leaves a squeeze that mix has to cover.A squeeze of 5 to 10 basis points a year
MixThe margin lever. Private label costs the contractor about 20% less, yet it carries a higher gross margin. EMEA's margin rose from 7.4% in 2015 to about 11% in 2024 as private label reached a quarter or more of its HVAC sales. North America is at the start of that road and is paying the entry cost now.The main source of margin gains
Cost-outSmall. About SEK 25m to 30m more of savings lands in 2027. A second European programme, under the chief executive who ran the first, has a plausible 35 to 40% chance by the end of 2027.A second programme would be worth SEK 75m to 150m a year
Financial leverageAdds and subtracts in similar amounts. Deals yield about 12 to 13% before tax against debt at about 4.5 to 5%, which adds 2.5 to 3.5% a year to EPS; rising interest takes back 2 to 3%.Roughly neutral
Accounting for sellers' stakesEPS flatters the economics slightly. Stakes of 10 to 25% left with sellers are consolidated at 100%, and the later cost of buying them goes through cash and equity, not through the income statement.An unrecorded financing cost of about 3 to 4% of EPS

One reinforcing loop drives the compounding, and one balancing loop sets its speed. Each acquisition adds branch density, purchasing volume and an outlet for private label and own-manufactured systems. Working capital, the leverage ceiling and the cash calls from option liabilities hold that loop to a steady speed.

Inference. Revenue growth produces roughly proportional, not outsized, profit growth: EBITA grows 1 to 2 points a year faster than revenue, and EPS a little faster again because the share count is flat. Beijer Ref compounds by deploying capital, not by levering a fixed cost base, which is why the balance sheet sets the speed of its growth.

So what. Do not expect margin-led upgrades; expect steadiness. The acquisition "firepower" is narrower than the reported leverage of 2.0x suggests: leverage is about 2.3x at the seasonal peak in Q2 2027, and about 2.8x once the option liabilities are counted. The 2026 pace of acquisitions cannot repeat without a release of inventory, a higher leverage ceiling or new equity.
Strongest counter-case. If North America follows the EMEA precedent, private label alone is worth 100 basis points or more of regional margin over several years, and a US housing recovery would add volume to a newly expanded branch network. One reading on AlphaSense has group margins at 13 to 14% by 2028.
What would change my view. A North American margin up by more than 50 basis points year on year for two consecutive quarters, with Sinclair in all 130 branches; or a group incremental margin above 20% in a quarter of normal weather.
Against the market. DNB Carnegie models about 40 basis points of margin gain a year; the model has 10 to 20. Without inflation, the precedents are lower: Ferguson targets 10 to 30 basis points, Rexel delivered 22, and Watsco's gross margin fell. Both visible brokers also use the reported leverage ratio, and neither discusses the second-quarter peak or the option liabilities.

Score: 40, set by the Rater. Structurally little gearing: incremental margins of about 10-12.5% sit at the average margin, organic drop-through is 15-20% (8.3% organic growth brought a lower underlying margin), price is pass-through of about 2% with a 5-10bp wage squeeze, cost-out is SEK 25-30m, and debt-funded deals add 2.5-3.5% a year to EPS while rising interest takes back 2-3%, so EPS grows about 1.2 times revenue against the Universe's typical 2 times. Above the distributor floor (Bravida, MITIE) because private-label mix has a proven EMEA record (7.4% to 11% margin) and acquisitions feed a density and purchasing loop, but that loop is governed by working capital and the leverage ceiling; coherent with the Economic strength (48) and Financial forecasts (53) groups, held lower because neither describes gearing.

6Forecast financials

Conclusion: the forecasts show a steady compounder of EPS at about 12% a year, with over half of the next two years' growth already signed; the path is faster than the recent past, and slower than consensus but better founded.

Signed acquisitions supply over half of the rise in EPS to FY2027, and organic growth adds nothing to the acceleration in revenue growth. Of the roughly 27% rise in EPS from FY2025 to FY2027, about 55% comes from acquisitions already signed (net of their interest), about 30% from organic growth, about 8% from margin and about 8% from acquisitions not yet announced, less about 5% for currency. Revenue growth accelerates by 8.4 points between 2025 and 2027, and almost all of that acceleration is the end of the currency drag (5.7 points) and the step-up in acquisitions (2.5 points).

Cash and the balance sheet.

  • Free cash flow has two honest definitions. On the first, the existing business generates about SEK 2.7bn in FY2027 after capital spending and lease principal (SEK 5.3 a share, a 3.4% yield). On the same definition FY2026 is nearer SEK 1.9bn to 2.0bn than the SEK 2.3bn cross-check, because the company stocked up ahead of the 2027 quota step. The second definition, the model's equity free cash flow (SEK 821m, 1,248m, 1,682m, 2,321m and 2,564m for FY2026 to FY2030), also pays for the working capital of the businesses bought.
  • Year-end net debt is about SEK 11.3bn to 11.4bn, not the model's SEK 13.9bn. The model's end-2026 figure (2.64x EBITDA) adds a full year of acquisitions and dividend in the fourth quarter on top of a Q3 balance that already contains them. The corrected figure is about 2.2x EBITDA including leases and about 1.9x on the company's definition, and leverage holds at 1.9x to 2.0x thereafter. End note 3 sets out the fix to the model.

Inference: is the growth double-digit, and is it better than the past?

  • Double-digit: yes. Revenue grows about 10% a year and EPS about 12% a year from 2026 to 2030.
  • Against 2023 to 2025: clearly better. EPS grew only about 3% a year then, held back by a 22% rise in the share count and by the krona.
  • Against 2019 to 2025: slower but cleaner. Revenue growth is about 10% a year against 16.6%; margin gains are about 15 basis points a year against about 60; and there is no dilution, against a 22% rise in the share count.
  • Why the path is plausible. The forecasts ask the company to repeat what it did from 2024 to 2026, not to improve on it. They do not need a return above target, a release of working capital, real pricing, a US housing recovery in 2027 or a second cost programme. Each of those is upside that the forecasts leave out.
So what. The earnings path can carry a return of about 12% a year on its own. What the earnings path cannot do is close the gap to consensus in FY2027.
Strongest counter-case. Upside: if organic growth holds at 5% and the margin rises 40 basis points a year, EPS compounds at about 15% a year (DNB Carnegie's view). Downside: without the acquisitions not yet announced, EPS is about SEK 6.4 in FY2027 and about SEK 6.9 in FY2028, growth of roughly 9% a year.
What would change my view. The five judgements of topic 9. The first tests are Q4 organic growth and year-end leverage, reported on 29 January 2027.
Where I lean differently, without changing an input. The model's Q3 2027 margin of 11.2% is at the cautious end. In Q3 2023, against the hot summer of 2022, organic growth was -4.4%, yet EMEA held its margin at 12.0%. I think a Q3 2027 margin of 11.4% to 11.5% is as likely; the difference is under 1% of FY2027 EPS, too small and too uncertain to justify changing an input.
Against the market. The model is in line with consensus for FY2026. For FY2027 it is 4 to 6% below consensus EPS like for like. For FY2028 it is 2.6% above consensus on revenue, because consensus carries no new deals, but 2 to 4.5% below on EPS, because the missing deals come with interest and the model's margin path is slower. The disagreement with consensus is about the composition of growth, not about the business: the model has less organic growth and margin, and more acquisitions and interest.

Score: 77, set by the Rater. About 11.5% sits in the 10-15% B band, low in it, and I place it near the floor because about half the growth is bought (signed and unannounced deals) on 3-5% organic, and the margin rises only 10-20bp a year against about 60bp a year in 2019-25, though it is clearly better than the 3% a year of 2023-25 and needs no dilution.

Conclusion: the scope for upgrades over the next 6 to 12 months is modest and V-shaped: favourable on revenue and acquisitions, unfavourable on FY2027 EPS, with the better-skewed moment arriving after the Q3 2027 report.

Evidence.

About 3% of the gap between the model and consensus can surface as cuts. The bridge below runs from DNB Carnegie's FY2027 EPS of SEK 6.76 to ours on the same basis (SEK 6.44 after minorities). Brokers strip transaction costs out of their EPS, so the SEK 0.13 of the gap that transaction costs explain will never show as a cut.

Almost half of the odds are on a cut of 2% or more to FY2027 consensus EPS. The chance that FY2027 results meet or beat today's consensus is about one in four on the earnings cone; I would allow up to one in three, because warm summers have been more common than cool ones.

Deals upgrade revenue more than EPS. Over twelve months, consensus for FY2027 has risen 8% on sales, 6% on EBITDA and 3% on EPS. Acquisitions arrive with interest, so the market's favourite mechanism for upgrades reaches the bottom line at well under full strength.

Inference. Over the next 6 to 12 months, the scope for EPS upgrades is limited, and slightly negative for FY2027; the scope for revenue upgrades is good; and the scope for guidance upgrades is small but not nil (topic 4). A narrative upgrade is available, but it is a different one from the one the sell-side expects: a returns agenda, not higher growth targets.

What the narrative does not yet hold: negative for the next 18 months

Rising interest, the option liabilities, the second-quarter leverage peak and the size of the dip in the Q3 2027 print.

What the narrative does not yet hold: positive beyond 18 months

The 2029 ban on split air-to-air units, the pay-off from private label, a release of working capital and the easy comparisons of 2028.
So what. Do not read confirmation in January and April as a de-risking of FY2027. Both reports face easy comparisons, and the driver that decides the year cannot be observed until July to October. The first report also opens with noise: a headline revenue "miss" that is only the timing of a deal, and about a one-in-four chance of a house-cleaning charge.
Strongest counter-case. Consensus is roughly our case plus one favourable draw. A warm summer (+3%) or a krona 6% weaker (+3%) would each close the gap; deals at 2026's pace would add about 1% to FY2027 EPS and 3% to FY2028; and any two of these together would produce upgrades. And because DNB Carnegie has already told its readers that the Q3 comparison is hard, a Q3 2027 print of zero may beat the market's fear even as it misses the model.
What would change my view. Organic growth above 6% in Q4 2026 and Q1 2027; FG Europe closed and another sizeable deal signed by April; EUR/SEK above 11.5.
Against the market. Sell-side momentum is pinned at the top grade, A, and the market extrapolates it. I expect the breadth of revisions to turn negative around the July and October 2027 reports and positive again into 2028.

Score: 40, set by the Rater. Guidance, which counts most, is likely only reaffirmed on 29 January (about three in four; a raised margin corridor 10-15%); FY2027 consensus is 4-6% above the model like for like, of which about 3% can surface as cuts at the July and October 2027 reports inside the window, partly offset by unmodelled deals at +1-1.5% per SEK 1bn, so the likely change is about -1 to -2%, roughly -0.15 times the 10% revenue growth rate (near the 35th percentile); the narrative is priced, with financing negatives unarticulated. Coherent with the fourth-set group's 40; below Tele2's limited further upgrades, a little above IMCD's.

8Current momentum: guidance, sell-side, narrative, share price and peers

Conclusion: Beijer Ref's momentum is strong in estimates, narrative and share price, absent in guidance and mixed among peers, and the share-price move looks like a completed catch-up to the Swedish serial acquirers.

Evidence.

Change over1 month3 months6 months12 months
Consensus FY2027 EPS+5%+8%+9%
Mean target price+4%+5%+8%
Share price+14.9%+27.4%+6.4%
  • Guidance: none. No target has been raised; the only recent changes tightened the framework.
  • Sell-side: strong. Consensus FY2028 EPS has risen a little more than FY2027. Buy ratings make up 75% of the total, up 8 points in six months. After Q3, Jefferies raised its 2027 and 2028 EPS by 4% and 7% and its target to SEK 190; DNB Carnegie raised its EPS by about 2% and held its target at SEK 170. The mean target of SEK 175 is 12% above the share price.
  • Narrative: strong. Brokers say "the compounder model is back on track", and the stock has a place on Jefferies' list of mid-cap top picks.
  • Share price: strong but young. The price is 14.9% above its 200-day average, but that average has risen in only one of the last twelve months. The relative-strength percentile is 76, and technical momentum is pinned at a B grade.
  • Peers: split. Among the Swedish serial acquirers, sell-side momentum is graded A for Indutrade, Lagercrantz and OEM International, but technical momentum is graded D for Addtech, Lagercrantz and OEM International, and twelve-month returns run from 0% to +10%. In the industry, Watsco has de-rated from 22x to 16x EV/EBITDA since May and Lennox from 16x to 11x, and NIBE, Ariston and Carrier have cut their margin guidance.

Inference. Beijer Ref's momentum is real and specific to the company: the six-month move maps onto the company's own dated events, while the Swedish serial acquirers went sideways and its industry peers fell.

Over twelve months, however, the stock has earned only the Swedish serial acquirers' return, and at 22.8x it now trades level with Indutrade (22.9x), the Swedish acquirer closest to it in returns. The share-price move is therefore more a completed catch-up than an established trend. Across the group, estimates are rising while prices lag, which is what a rising discount rate looks like.

So what. Momentum supports the shares for the next few months, but the stock now has less protection against a de-rating of the Swedish serial acquirers than it had in May, when its own discount to them was still there to absorb one.
Strongest counter-case. A newly restarted acquisition engine in a short-cycle upturn is exactly what has worked in this sector: Indutrade's shares rose about 40% after its organic growth turned. And a stock that has only matched its peer group over a year is not extended.
What would change my view. A 200-day average rising for three months or more, together with improving technical grades across the Swedish serial acquirers, would indicate a trend rather than a catch-up.
Against the market. I agree that momentum is strong today. I differ on its durability into mid-2027, because the dated dip in organic growth arrives just as the easy part of the catch-up is spent.

Score: 81, set by the Rater. Both measures positive and none strongly negative gives B; placed in the upper part of the band because revisions are strong (FY2027 EPS +8% and +9% over three and six months, p87 and p82, about 0.8 times revenue growth), 75% Buy and rising, Jefferies top pick, and the price is 15% above its 200-day average, but held off the A by relative strength short of the top fifth, a 200-day average that has risen in only one of twelve months, no guidance raise, and industry peers de-rating.

9Riskiness and simplicity of the forecasts and expectations

Conclusion: Beijer Ref's business risk is moderate, simple to describe and well cushioned; the share-price risk is larger, and it sits in two drivers the company does not control (the weather and the krona) and in a multiple set by the Swedish serial acquirers as a group.

Simplicity: the case is simple at the top and blurred lower down. Three drivers explain the earnings: acquired sales (announced deal by deal), organic volume and the krona, and the company publishes sensitivities for currency and interest rates. The trace blurs between EBITA and EPS. There are four EPS bases for FY2025 (SEK 4.59 to about 5.08, an 11% spread), brokers disagree on the path of interest, and the option liabilities sit outside both net debt and EPS.

The five judgements, with the arithmetic.

1. The summer of 2027 is normal, so Q3 2027 organic growth is about -0.5%.

  • Plausible error: 4 points either way. After the hot summer of 2022, Q3 2023 organic growth was -4.4%; a repeat of 2026's heat would give about +3.5%. As a rough cross-check, 2023 gave back about a quarter of 2022's +18.6% spike, and the same ratio applied to +8.3% gives about -2%.
  • Revenue. 4% of Q3 2026 revenue of SEK 11,641m is SEK 466m, or 1.0% of FY2027 revenue; FY2027 organic growth becomes 2.1% or 4.1% instead of 3.1%.
  • EBITA. At a 25% drop-through on volume in the peak quarter, the swing is SEK 116m, or 2.3% of FY2027 EBITA; the Q3 margin becomes 10.7% or 11.7% instead of 11.2%.
  • EPS. SEK 116m less 24.5% tax is SEK 88m; over 507m shares that is SEK 0.17, or 2.7% of SEK 6.51. At a 15% drop-through, which the way up suggests, it is SEK 0.10, or 1.6%.

2. The krona stays near EUR/SEK 11.2.

  • Plausible error: 5% either way, and 10% in a rate shock. Bank forecasts for 2027 run from 10.70 to 11.15.
  • EBIT. The company's sensitivity is SEK 221m for a 10% move against the euro and the dollar, so SEK 110m for 5%, or 2.2% of FY2027 EBITA. Revenue moves by about SEK 2bn for a 5% move if all currencies move together, since 98% of sales are outside Sweden's currency.
  • EPS. SEK 110m less tax is SEK 83m; over 507m shares that is SEK 0.16, or 2.5%. For a 10% move it is SEK 0.33, or 5.1%.
  • The one correlated case is a krona rally driven by interest rates. Add 50 basis points on largely floating debt (SEK 51m, or SEK 0.08 a share) and the total is about -SEK 0.24, or -3.7% of EPS, with the multiples of the Swedish serial acquirers falling at the same time.

3. Acquisitions not yet announced add SEK 2.0bn of sales in 2027 and SEK 2.5bn a year after, bought at about 0.85x sales.

  • Per SEK 1bn of acquired sales. EBITA at about 11% is SEK 110m; the price is SEK 850m; interest at 4.8% is SEK 41m; pre-tax profit is SEK 69m and after-tax profit SEK 52m; EPS rises SEK 0.10, or 1.4% of FY2028 EPS.
  • If the price is 1.2x sales. Interest is SEK 58m, pre-tax profit SEK 52m and the EPS gain SEK 0.08. The same borrowing also buys about 30% fewer sales.
  • If deals pause. FY2027 EPS falls by about 1% and FY2028 EPS by about 5% (SEK 0.36); FY2028 revenue is about SEK 47.0bn instead of SEK 50.1bn.
  • If 2026's pace repeats (SEK 3.7bn a year). FY2028 gains about SEK 2.3bn more of full-year sales and EPS rises SEK 0.23, or 3%. But that pace needs SEK 2.5bn to 3.5bn more debt, which takes year-end leverage to about 2.4x to 2.5x and above the ceiling at the second-quarter peak. Upside on this line therefore needs a release of inventory or new equity; downside needs nothing.

4. Net interest rises to SEK 600m in 2027 and SEK 685m in 2028.

  • Consensus implies SEK 504m and SEK 414m. The 2028 difference of SEK 271m, less tax, is SEK 205m, or SEK 0.40 a share: 5.4% of consensus FY2028 EPS. For 2027 the difference is SEK 96m, SEK 0.14 a share, or 2.1%.
  • If I am wrong. One point on interest rates is worth SEK 102m (the company's sensitivity), SEK 0.15 a share, or 2.3%. If the business needs less borrowing than the forecasts assume, as the cash lines in the earlier answer sets suggest it might, 2028 interest is about SEK 50m lower: +SEK 0.07, or +1%.

5. The EBITA margin rises 10 to 20 basis points a year from mix.

  • 10 basis points on FY2028 revenue of SEK 50,139m is SEK 50m; after tax SEK 38m, or SEK 0.07 a share (1.0%).
  • DNB Carnegie's margin path is 30 basis points higher by 2028: SEK 150m, SEK 0.22 a share, or 3.1%.
  • A second European cost programme of SEK 75m to 150m adds SEK 0.11 to 0.22 a share (1.5 to 3%), at a one-off cost of about one to one-and-a-half times the annual saving.

The earnings cone: eight outcomes in ten fall within about 6% of SEK 6.51. Taken as independent, the five drivers give a standard deviation of a little under 5%. That width matches the range consensus itself has shown over the last year. The body of the distribution is symmetrical; the left tail is heavier because of the correlated rate case in judgement 2. The share price has a partial natural hedge: the krona tends to weaken in risk-off markets, which adds to translated earnings just when multiples are under pressure. The hedge fails only in the rate-driven case.

Sudden risks: none breaks the thesis on its own.

RiskPlausibility over 18 monthsSize
A write-down of legacy stock in the refrigerant transitionLow5% of about SEK 12bn of inventory is SEK 600m, about 15% of a year's pre-tax profit, one-off
A control failure in a subsidiary (there is no internal audit; Indutrade's UK case cost SEK 125m)Low to moderateSEK 50m to 200m; larger for sentiment
Short-seller attention to the option liabilities and controls (Lifco's shares fell 16% in such an episode)Low to moderateA multiple event, not an earnings one
An equity-funded US platform dealAbout 15% over four yearsDilution, as in 2023
A charge in the new chief executive's first reportAbout one in fourSEK 100m to 200m, outside adjusted EPS

Trackability: disclosure is good on what happened and thin on what was earned from what. The company reports organic growth by region and segment, each deal's sales and the effects of currency. It gives no guidance, no split of price and volume, no order figures, no prices paid for deals and no maturity schedule for the option liabilities. The calendar is back to front: the two reports in the next six months face easy comparisons, and the fragility is not tested until July and October 2027. Three markers are worth holding:

  • Q4 2026 organic growth below +3% would be a warning.
  • Year-end leverage above 2.1x on the company's definition would tighten the constraint on deals in 2027.
  • EUR/SEK at 10.70 would take about 2% off FY2027 EPS.

Share-price risk. With earnings intact, a fall to the five-year low multiple (18.85x) or to the ten-year tenth percentile (17.4x) means a share-price fall of 17 to 24%; with EPS 10% lower as well, the fall is about 26 to 31%. The brokers' own bear cases are SEK 100 to 120.

Precedents.

  • The multiple usually falls before the hard comparison prints, and brokers cut their estimates after it. Watsco and Pool de-rated in 2022 before their earnings fell; Lennox's shares fell 8.8% on the day it reported a beat driven by pre-buying; NIBE's fell 27% in 2023. Beijer Ref's own multiple fell from about 35x in March 2023 to about 20x in October 2023 (the rights issue and EQT's placing were part of the cause), and brokers cut EPS by about 8% only after the Q3 2023 print.
  • Three things separated the cases the market looked through: continuing acquisitions, regulation-driven demand and a margin that held. Beijer Ref has all three, and it starts from 22x, not 35x. Against that, 60% of its sales are in EMEA and 62% in comfort cooling, so it cannot dilute the effect of the summer the way Daikin could.
So what. Beijer Ref's risks have handles and dates. The earnings risk is the smaller part and is trackable. The price risk is the larger part, and on the precedents it peaks between April and October 2027, ahead of the Q3 print rather than at it.
Strongest counter-case. Riskier than I say: three negatives share one cause (interest rates), all-in leverage is 2.8x and there is no internal audit, so one bad event could bring an episode like Lifco's. Safer than I say: the margin has held in every downturn on record, and the aftermarket base does not go away.
What would change my view. Simpler and safer: a maturity schedule for the option liabilities and a weather-adjusted growth figure. Riskier: a move in the krona of more than 5%, which would dominate every other driver.
Against the market. The market knows the risks in outline, as the brokers' downside cases show. What is missing is the arithmetic: no visible broker models Q3 2027 organic growth at zero, 2028 interest above 2027's, or leverage including the option liabilities.

Score: 59, set by the Rater. The earnings case is simple and cushioned: three drivers, an FY2027 EPS cone of about plus or minus 6% (80% interval), no single assumption above about 3%, and a margin that has held in every downturn; but the swing drivers (summer weather, the krona, rates) are outside the company's control and untestable until July-October 2027, the left tail is fattened by a correlated rate shock, all-in leverage is about 2.8x with SEK 3.4bn of option liabilities and no internal audit across 170 subsidiaries, and the share-price range (17-31% to low multiples) is about three times the earnings range. Coherent with the Risks groups (58 and 63); below Banca Generali, above NKT's concentrated ramp-up risk.

10Where the stock is in its lifecycle

Conclusion: Beijer Ref is in the thesis-broadening phase on fundamentals and further ahead on expectations, and the mechanical dip in organic growth in the second half of 2027 should be read as a pause, not as a stall.

Evidence.

  • On fundamentals, the case has turned up and is broadening. Organic growth, acquisitions, leadership and ownership all moved the right way between June and October 2026, and estimates are rising on more than one driver.
  • On expectations, the stock already behaves as if the case were reinforcing. Estimates have risen for six months, 75% of ratings are Buy, the price is 15% above its 200-day average, and the stock's discount to its nearest peer, Indutrade, has closed.
  • Ahead lies a dated, mechanical pause. Organic growth of about zero in Q3 2027 will come with FY2027 estimates drifting down by about 3% through the summer.

Inference. I agree with the dashboard's starting phase of Broadening, with two qualifications. First, by the measure of expectations, the stock is late in that phase: the market has moved faster than the fundamentals. Second, the next phase is not automatic. Over the next eighteen months, my odds are about one in two that the case passes through the 2027 pause into a reinforcing phase in 2028 (deals continue, the margin holds and a returns agenda appears); about one in three that it stalls for a year or so (the pause meets a de-rating of the Swedish serial acquirers, and the multiple settles at 19x to 21x); and about one in six that the thesis itself is damaged (by a pause in deals, a control failure or a US margin that does not recover).

So what. When a broadening thesis has a known pause ahead, timing matters more than usual. The pause is not a reason to doubt the business; it is a reason to expect a better-skewed entry point than today's somewhere between the spring and the autumn of 2027, unless the multiple falls first.
Strongest counter-case. The market may simply look through a pause it has been warned about, as it did for Daikin. In that case the phase is already reinforcing, and waiting costs the earnings growth in between, about 1% a month.
What would change my view. Toward reinforcing: organic growth above 4% through a summer of normal weather. Toward a stall: a pause in deals announced together with the second-quarter leverage peak.
Against the market. The sell-side places the stock at the start of a new earnings cycle. I place it in the same phase but further through it, with the easy part of the re-rating done.

Score: 58, set by the Rater. The computed and memo Broadening is right on fundamentals (organic turn, deals, owner, CEO all moved June-October 2026), but late on expectations: six months of upgrades, 75% Buy, +27% in six months and the discount to Indutrade closed, with a dated pause ahead (Q3 2027 organic about zero, FY2027 estimates drifting down about 3%) and the memo's odds of one in two reinforcing, one in three stall, one in six damage. Late Broadening with the good news known: below Nexans' paused Reinforcing because the pause is still to come, just above Greggs.

11The fair multiple

Conclusion: the guideline's fair multiple of 34.26x describes an interest-rate regime that has gone, and 24x to 26x is the multiple the evidence supports while Beijer Ref delivers.

The guideline. Viewforth's guideline sets the fair multiple for a stock in the Broadening phase at the 80th percentile of the stock's own ten-year history, which for Beijer Ref is 34.26x two-year-forward earnings. That multiple is 50% above the 22.8x from which the model starts (end note 6). Topic 12 uses it.

My view: 34.26x is too high for Beijer Ref in this phase. I would use 24x to 26x while the company is delivering, and 19x to 21x in a stall.

Evidence.

The ten-year history of the multiple spans three different regimes (monthly series in the files):

PeriodMedianRangeWhat set the multiple
October 2016 to December 201920.3x17.3x to 32.6xA European wholesaler; a rising margin; low interest rates
January 2020 to March 202336.9x21.4x to 57.8xNear-zero interest rates; EBITA compounding at 38% a year under EQT; the period before the rights issue
April 2023 to September 202624.6x19.8x to 29.7xAfter the Heritage acquisition and a 22% rise in the share count; higher interest rates; returns below target
  • Every one of the 27 months at or above 34.26x fell between May 2020 and March 2023. The 80th percentile therefore describes that one regime. To reach 34.26x by March 2028, the stock would have to trade 15% above the highest month-end multiple it has reached since April 2023 (29.7x).
  • The Swedish serial acquirers do not command 34x. Those with about twice Beijer Ref's return on capital trade at 26x to 27x; Indutrade, the one closest to Beijer Ref in returns, trades at 22.9x.
  • Interest rates are rising, not falling, and in this sector compounders de-rate together when yields rise.
  • Even the optimists stop well short of 34x. Broker targets of SEK 170 to 190 are 25x to 28x today's two-year-forward consensus EPS.

Inference. For Beijer Ref, reversion to normal means reversion to the post-2023 regime (about 24.6x) or, generously, to the ten-year median (26.2x). Either is 8 to 15% above today's multiple, not 50%. For a business growing EPS at about 12% a year with a return on capital of 11%, 24x to 26x is already a full price.

So what. The multiple can contribute to the return, but as a tailwind worth about a tenth, not as the main event.
Strongest counter-case. The stock reached 32.6x in 2019, before EQT, on rising margins and hot summers. A returns agenda under the new owner, a clean share register, the 2029 ban reaching the largest segment and falling yields could together justify a multiple in the high twenties. I would treat about 30x, the post-2023 peak, as the ceiling in a reinforcing phase.
What would change my view. Return on operating capital above 13% with inventory below 140 days; the US ten-year yield back under 4.5%; or a re-rating of the Swedish serial acquirers.
Against the market. The market pays about 22x to 23x; the brokers argue for 25x to 28x; the guideline says 34x. I sit slightly above the market and at the low end of the brokers.

Score: 58, set by the Rater. Neutral on both gives C; placed a little above mid-band because the memo's supportable 24-26x delivery multiple and the post-2023 regime median of 24.6x sit 5-14% above today, but held down because the 35th percentile is flattered by the 2020-23 regime that set the top of the range, and the stock no longer trades at a discount to its nearest peer.

To 31 March 2028 (the 18-month column)+82.5%+54.1%SEK 288.85+19.9%+50.4%+2.2%
To 30 September 2029 (the three-year column)+113.1%+29.9%SEK 337.41+39.4%+50.4%+3.5%

What drives each part of the return.

  • Earnings. Two-year-forward EPS rises from about SEK 6.9 to about SEK 8.3 by March 2028 and to about SEK 9.7 by September 2029: about 12% a year, the compounding rate of topic 6. The first leg is well founded, since over half of the growth to FY2027 is signed, with one qualification: about a third of the 18-month earnings gain rests on acquisitions not yet announced.
  • The multiple. The move from 22.8x to 34.26x supplies +50.4% on both horizons, and it compounds with the earnings gain. The multiple is three-fifths of the 18-month return and a little under half of the three-year return.
  • Dividends and other cash returns. Dividends total SEK 3.50 a share over the first horizon and SEK 5.55 over the second, and there are no buybacks. The cash that might have been returned (a free cash flow yield of about 3.4% from the existing business) goes into acquisitions instead, so it reaches shareholders as EPS growth of about 2.5 to 3.5% a year inside the earnings leg.

My reading: the same earnings at other multiples.

Multiple at the horizonTo 31 March 2028To 30 September 2029
34.26x (guideline)+82.5%+113.1% (about 30% a year)
26.2x (ten-year median)about +40%about +64% (about 18% a year)
24x (post-2023 regime)about +28%about +50% (about 15% a year)
22.8x (unchanged)about +22%about +43% (about 13% a year)
19x (stall)about +2%about +20% (about 6% a year)
17.4x (ten-year tenth percentile)about -6%about +10%
  • With my own rough weights, the 18-month return is about +24%, roughly 16% a year. The weights are 45% on delivery with steady multiples for the Swedish serial acquirers (24x to 26x), 30% on an unchanged multiple and 25% on a stall at 19x to 21x.
  • If earnings also miss or beat by 6%: 19x on EPS 6% lower gives about -4%; 26.2x on EPS 6% higher gives about +48%.
  • Over the next six months (my arithmetic, not the model's): forward EPS rolls up about 6% and the dividend adds 1%, so an unchanged multiple gives about +7%, 24x to 25x gives +13% to +17%, and 20x gives about -6%.

Inference. Earnings growth plus the dividend, about 13 to 14% a year, is the dependable part of the return. Over 18 months the multiple can add or remove a similar amount, so the 18-month outcome is mostly a view on the multiple. Over three years the earnings leg dominates and the range of outcomes narrows. The horizon therefore changes the character of the investment: at 18 months it is a position on the rating of the Swedish serial acquirers; at three years it is a claim on a compounding machine.

Strongest counter-case. If the guideline is right about the phase, and the market pays for delivery as it did before 2023, the return is far above mine. If the Swedish serial acquirers de-rate while organic growth pauses, 18 months of earnings growth is spent standing still.
What would change my view. The same things that would change the fair multiple (topic 11), plus a pace of deals above the base, funded without debt, which would lift the earnings leg.
Against the market. Brokers' targets imply returns of 9 to 22% over twelve months. My central reading is close to theirs; the model at the guideline multiple is far above both.

Score: 77, set by the Rater. About +24% sits in the B band (about 79 on the scale) and the three-year check supports it; I move it down two for the skew, because the left tail is fatter than the body (a stall at 19-21x gives about nil, with a 6% EPS miss about -4%, and the rate shock hits earnings and multiple together), while the model's +82.5% rests on a 34x multiple the evidence does not support.

13Summary conclusion

Beijer Ref is a good business having a good year, and the investment case is cleaner than it was in September. The organic engine has turned in the reported numbers; the acquisition engine is running above its normal pace; the chief executive's chair is filled by the operator of the best region; and a private-equity seller has given way to an industrial owner whose habits point at the company's two real weaknesses, returns and working capital. The forecasts ask the company only to repeat what it has done, and more than half of the EPS growth to 2027 is already signed.

What the case lacks today is a gap between what we believe and what the market expects. The positives are known and largely in the price. Like for like, our FY2027 EPS is below consensus. The under-discussed items are financing items that lean negative. And the one quarter that cannot be observed for eight months, the summer of 2027, is reported just after the easy part of the news flow. None of this damages the business; all of it shapes the timing of an entry.

The practical reading for the next 12 to 24 months:

What to believe:
EPS growth of about 12% a year with a narrow cone, and a margin that holds through the pause.
What not to pay for:
a multiple above the mid-twenties, or an upgrade of the growth targets.
What would make the skew unusually positive:
a target for returns or working capital; a multiple near 19x to 20x; the Q3 2027 report behind us; or deals funded by a release of inventory.
What to watch, in order of importance:
29 January 2027 (the tone on returns, leverage and any charge); the krona; deal announcements and what they imply about prices paid; trading in June and July 2027; and the annual report's note on option liabilities.

The four memo ratings.

65
Thesis's Change Forces' Strength
65, set by the Rater.
The input forces are clearly but partly positive (external 65: law-dated regulation on 40-45% of sales, half the organic turn weather; internal 64: owner, CEO and re-lit deals, ambition unchanged), and they reach profits surely but at an ordinary rate, about 11.5% EPS growth (B) with over half of the growth to FY2027 already signed but little organic or margin step-up, so the net change is a firm mid-60s positive rather than the 75+ that a growth or margin step well above the typical company would earn.
63
Foundations' Robustness
63, set by the Rater.
The value chain and business are robust (number one in Europe, 80-90% aftermarket, widening regulatory and private-label moats, a margin held through the 2023-25 stall and the 2020 fall), which on Richard's CVS reasoning lifts stability above the ordinary quality score of 57, but returns near the cost of capital on new deals, about 40% working capital, all-in leverage about 2.8x, governance below the cohort and a mixed delivery record (topic 4 at 49) keep it well short of the 75-80 band.
70
Setups' Fit/Crispness
70, set by the Rater.
In substance the case is a recognisable 'Delivering - Serial Acquirer - Mechanical EPS Upgrader': a re-lit deal engine adding about 10% of revenue a year, signed deals carrying over half of near-term EPS growth, and unmodelled M&A as the standing upgrade source; but one element is loose today, since deals now earn only about 7-9% on new capital, arrive with rising interest so upgrades reach EPS at well under full strength, and the leverage ceiling governs the pace, so it sits just below 75 (the FY2027 consensus gap and the price already paid are timing, scored in 7 and 12, not here).
62
Case Riskiness
62, set by the Rater.
The earnings risks are close to Richard's 'paper cuts' (plus or minus 6% on FY2027, a margin that has held in every downturn) and the multiple is in the lower half of its ten-year range, which lifts it a little above topic 9's 59, but the swing drivers are exogenous and untestable until mid-2027, there is no guidance to manage the sell-side, all-in leverage is about 2.8x with a control-failure tail, and the share-price range is three times the earnings range under a cohort de-rating risk.

End notes: bases, sources and corrections

  1. The forecasts are the Financial Analyst's model (model update 1). EPS is stated before amortisation of acquired intangibles and after transaction costs. I change no forecast input, so there is no file of changed inputs.
  2. Bases of EPS. The FactSet consensus EPS mixes brokers who add back the amortisation of acquired intangibles with brokers who do not; multiply the FactSet median by about 1.026 to compare it with our figures. The model does not deduct minority interests (SEK 0.05 to 0.07 a share); after minorities, EPS is SEK 5.75, 6.44 and 7.21 for FY2026 to FY2028. The model summary shows FY2026 EPS growth of +23.9% because it measures growth from a FactSet base of SEK 4.69, struck after the 2025 restructuring charge and after acquired amortisation; the like-for-like base is SEK 5.08.
  3. One correction to the model's balance sheet. The model overstates year-end net debt by about SEK 2.5bn to 3bn, a timing artefact (topic 6), and this memo quotes corrected leverage throughout. To fix the model, the Financial Analyst should enter in the reported quarters of FY2026 the acquisitions and dividend actually paid in them, so that year-end net debt starts from the reported SEK 11,703m at Q3 plus only what remains to be paid.
  4. The latest Earnings Review covers the quarter to September 2026. It reviews the report of 22 October 2026, and its net sales (SEK 11,641m) match FactSet's Q3 column, so I rely on it.
  5. EQT's exit. The ownership report written for this memo records EQT's placing of its remaining 30.7m B-shares on 18 June 2026. That record updates the earlier answer sets, which still carried EQT at 6.4%. The record rests on one news item and two broker comments, so it deserves a one-line check against the share register.
  6. Starting multiple. The guideline's 34.26x is 50% above the 22.8x from which the model starts, and 57% above the 21.8x on the Phases page's own series.

How to read this page

Every rating of this stock on one page: the Rater's 1-100 number, its letter and the Rater's own reason (at most three sentences, taken from the ratings file; nothing newly written). The number is the company's approximate standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10; 50 = typical). A letter follows its item's rule: rank among the stocks scored (A the top 10%; B+ and B the next 15%; C+, C and C- the next 25%; D the next 25%; F the bottom 25%); or Richard's cut-offs on the measure for the four numerical topics (forecast financials, current momentum, the fair multiple, total shareholder return). On the change-forces items the number carries a sign (50 = neither positive nor negative) and the letter is the rank, so read the two together. "9th of 30 stocks scored" is the stock's place on that item. A dashed badge is provisional (fewer than 30 stocks scored).
